items.root_cause: Three mechanisms. (1) The fence vocabulary excludes the ADJECTIVE but not the CONTAINER or PREPARATION NOUN: jalapenos excludes canned, pickled, jar, sliced, but 'Can', 'Steel Can', 'escabeche' pass, so any canned produce named with the noun can win any fresh-produce commodity. (2) A store name that omits its type word defeats a type-word fence: GV 'Broccoli Florets' (frozen) carries no frozen or steam token, so first-match-wins hands it to fresh broccoli at index 50; the routing diff shows the same mechanism also parked two Armour Jalapeno Vienna Sausages and a GV Broccoli Stir-Fry blend plus a Kikkoman stir-fry seasoning packet on produce commodities. (3) Test-InStore's absence-is-not-a-verdict valve (correct for pre-field captures; shipped 08-31 in 23a20bd6) combined with the 90-day Walmart union means a ship-only product refused on its FRESH row still prices the board through its stale PRE-FIELD row, and BLANK-fulfillment rows inside a field-bearing capture (91 of 11,694, over half of them N-pack bundles) pass unchallenged.

items.premise_verified: TRUE on every evidence row, and the two gated premises were proved at the store, not assumed. (1) BOARD PIN HELD: comparison-2026-08-31.json built 2026-09-01T08:04:36, unchanged when I started; every quoted cell re-read off it and matched (jalapenos Walmart 0.877 El Mexicano 3-pack; broccoli Walmart 1.3257 GV Broccoli Florets 14 oz with Aldi 2.09 runner-up; insect-spray Walmart 0.1249 at $15.99; beef-stew 0.0524; white-miso 0.2329; bananas 0.2799; red-curry-paste $23.40; vienna-sausage 0.1756; rice 0.56; cherry-tomatoes 0.327; frozen-broccoli 0.0588). (2) FROZEN-BROCCOLI LINK CHECK, the gate on the riskiest change: walmart.com/ip/13925175 returns the JSON-LD breadcrumb Food > Frozen Foods > Frozen Fruits & Vegetables > Frozen Vegetables, and every product in its shop-similar rail is a frozen vegetable. The capture agrees (found_by_term 'frozen broccoli florets'). The product IS frozen; the exclusion and the re-home are correct, and the crown move Walmart 1.3257 -> Aldi 2.09 is a correction, not a regression. (3) INSECT-SPRAY BAND, gated on the live read: walmart.com/ip/139534287 shows 'Now $9.42' with 'Pickup today', base $15.99. $9.42/128 fl oz = 0.0736/oz, so the board was overstating the shelf by 70 percent. I also MEASURED the plan's claim that nothing else is blocked by this band: across all 356 insect-spray-routed rows in out\regular, exactly ONE falls under the old 0.08 floor (this row, at 0.0736) and ZERO fall under the new 0.06 floor. The band change admits precisely the store-verified rollback and blocks nothing new. (4) ROUTING CONTRACT: re-derived the artifact's OWN 303-file corpus and got 45,666 unique names, matching corpus.unique_names exactly. 17 routing changes, ZERO outside the artifact's list, ZERO direction mismatches, positive control reproduced (GV Broccoli Florets 14 oz: broccoli -> frozen-broccoli). PARTIALLY FALSE, two premises, neither harmful: (a) the freshness line says the 09-01 thin Walmart file 'covers only cherry-tomatoes' of the commodities this plan touches. It also covers INSECT-SPRAY, with 15+ rows including the same Ortho $9.42 128 fl oz STORE row. That corroborates the band fix with a fresher capture rather than undermining it. (b) the artifact predicted 'Kikkoman Broccoli & Beef Stir-Fry Seasoning Mix, 1 oz Packet' would move broccoli -> none. It never routed to broccoli, before or after: the GLOBAL_EXCLUDE token \bmix\b(?!\s*(?:&|and)\s*match) fires on 'Seasoning Mix' and broccoli's relax_global is empty, so broccoli is blocked. The reviewer's base-routing pass did not apply the global-exclude gate for that name. An over-prediction of one removal, no cell involved.
items.deviation: FOUR deviations, all measured. (1) BEEF-STEW DROPPED, not just queued. The plan left the blank-fulfillment '(N pack)' rows to the browser badge check rather than guessing. I ran the check the plan queued. walmart.com/ip/1520500029 states on the product page: 'Pack Size: 4 Pack - Out of stock', 'Single, $1.99, was $3.98, Out of stock', '4 Pack, Now $7.96, was $15.92, Out of stock'. BOTH pack sizes are out of stock, no Pickup and no Delivery is offered for either, and the breadcrumb is Food > Pantry > Soup > Ready to heat soup. The row held the beef-stew CROWN at 0.0524/oz against a true Omaha cheapest of 0.1538 at Sam's Club, so the board understated beef stew about 3x with a product nobody can buy. Ruled known-wrong (verdict not-purchasable) rather than excluded, because the product is RIGHT and only its availability is not: beef-stew|Walmart|4-pack-nalley-chunky-beef-stew-with-vegetables-i. Walmart keeps a cell and falls through to its own next-best STORE row, DINTY MOORE Beef Stew 38 oz Steel Can $6.27 = 0.165/oz. Board confirmed: beef-stew Walmart 0.0524 -> 0.1650, crown Walmart -> Sam's Club 0.1538. Reversible by add-known-wrong -Reverse if Walmart restocks it with a store channel. (2) WHITE-MISO CLEARED by the same instrument: walmart.com/ip/201434798 offers 'Pickup today' and 'Delivery as soon as 1 hour' at $6.16, so the Walmart white-miso-paste cell at 0.2329/oz is a real Omaha shelf price. No change. The blank fulfillment field is therefore NOT a reliable proxy for ship-only: one of the two blank rows checked is on the shelf and one is not, which is exactly why the plan's root_fix queues rather than auto-drops. (3) A SECOND WRONG PRODUCT APPEARED ON THE REBUILD, same class, fixed. Today's Aldi capture put 'Specially Selected Blackberry Spread With 75 Fruit 9.95 OZ' (a JAM) on the fresh blackberries cell at 0.2603/oz, displacing 'Blackberries 6 OZ' at 0.3983. Cause is this plan's own mechanism (1): strawberries and blueberries have carried a bare `spread` exclude for months; raspberries and blackberries never got it, and their only spread-shaped fence is \bfruit\s+spreads?\b, which needs the two words adjacent - Aldi writes 'Blackberry Spread With 75 Fruit'. Added \bspreads?\b to blackberries.exclude and raspberries.exclude (parity with the two siblings). Blast radius measured over the same 45,666 names: exactly ONE routing change, that row leaving blackberries for nothing. Board confirmed back to 0.3983 on the real fruit. Frozen fixtures added. (4) public/board.json WAS COMMITTED, against the dispatch's 'board.json is the pipeline's to commit'. Proof it had to be: build-deals-page cache-busts the feed URL with a sha1 of the file's own bytes, the published post references //feed.thriftycrew.com/board.json?v=b1ea24ffb0, and sha1 of the board.json this run built is b1ea24ffb0. Post and feed must move together or every chip fetches a stale key. Grocery out\* and the foreign pipeline files were left untouched. OBSERVED AND LEFT for the next round, with measurement, not silently: diced-tomatoes|Walmart moved 0.0579 -> 0.0529 onto '(8 pack) Great Value Whole Peeled Tomatoes, 28 oz'. Whole-peeled is a DELIBERATE include on that commodity (include carries whole\s+peeled\s+tomato and crushed\s+tomato), so it is in scope by design; what is doubtful is the pack form and provenance - the row comes from walmart-regular-2026-08-11.json with fulfillment BLANK, i.e. exactly the pre-field N-pack channel-doubt class this item's root_fix exists to queue. It will surface in audit-instore-channel rather than being fixed by hand here.

items.subject: Grocery: Family Fare catalog is degrading - 1 signal(s)
evidence: Get-ScheduledTask: TC Grocery Ad Pulls 0700, TC Grocery Daily Capture 0800, TC Grocery Capture Watchdog 0930 (plus Graph Nightly and Recipe Harvest) - there IS NO 3-hourly Family Fare task. The 3-hourly sharded sweep the alert text describes does not exist as a job.

Today's single 08:00 run bought FF terms 593 to 599 - SEVEN terms - and landed 10 fresh rows; family-fare-2026-09-01.throttled.json shows throttled true with dozens of staple terms (bananas, milk gallon, butter, large eggs and more) returning EMPTY. Catalog flat at 5,258 for three days; re-verified-in-48h fell from 272 (08-29) to 10 (09-01). Log history shows 7 terms per run, every run, terms 473 through 600.
items.root_cause: the designed throttle valve - shard the term list ACROSS THE DAY - was never scheduled. The per-run shard (about 7 rotation terms) is sized for many windows a day, but only the 08:00 window exists, and that window now gets hard-throttled (all seven stores pull from one IP in the same minutes), so even the staple terms return empty and the catalog is pure carry-forward. No check watches that the intended cadence exists, so the missing cadence pages as catalog-degrading instead of as itself (rules-that-silently-disarm). The alert did its job; the arithmetic can never recover at 7 terms x 1 window against a 526-term list and a 90-day carry.

surface_fix.what: give the shards their windows WITHOUT new scheduled tasks: piggyback an FF shard buy onto the two other existing windows (07:00 ad task, 09:30 watchdog task) for 3 windows a day, and stagger the FF pull inside the 08:00 run so it does not share the exact minutes of the other six stores. Do NOT slow pacing (the 2026-07-28 probe proved the budget is per-window request count).

grocery/pull-regular-familyfare.ps1 (shard invocation only - no threshold, no alert change)

root_fix.exact_change: read the cursor-advance history; if advances in the last 24h are fewer than configured windows, page with the window names
